main_result: Every nonempty finite oriented graph D has a vertex v with |N_1^+(v)| <= |N_2^+(v)|, where N_1^+(v) is the out-neighbourhood and N_2^+(v) is the set of vertices at directed distance exactly two (Seymour's second neighbourhood conjecture). Corollaries give weighted forms (for every vertex weighting some v satisfies a weighted inequality; some weighting makes every vertex satisfy it; an arc-weighted version), and consequences for oriented graphs without directed triangles (a vertex with deg^+(v) <= |Non(v)|, n-1 >= 2deg^+(v)+deg^-(v), and a directed-triangle result under minimum in- and out-degree n/3).
proof_strategy: Proof by contradiction. (1) Lemma subset-deficit: in a minimal counterexample D (fewest vertices, then arcs), every nonempty proper S satisfies |F^2(S)\F(S)| < |F(S)\S|. This is shown by deleting arcs from S to E\T for a set T, using minimality to find a vertex v that loses an out-neighbour, and bounding the change in g(T) = |F(T)\(I∪T)| by an increment strictly less than |Y|; telescoping over T_0 ⊂ T_1 ⊂ ... ⊂ E gives g(E) < |E|. (2) Lemma blowup: replacing each vertex by a transitive tournament of size m > n transfers the strict subset inequality to a graph G with |U| + |F_G^2(U)| < 2|F_G(U)| for all proper nonempty U; the case S = V(D) is handled separately using positive indegree. (3) Proposition no-concavity: for such G, take a compatible pair (P,Q) of arc-image families maximizing |P|+|Q|+d; the strict inequalities on columns and rows give larger complementary families R, C that are not compatible; a pruning lemma (proved via König's theorem and a generic-rank argument producing a real assignment satisfying three rank conditions) deletes at most |H|+q members, which yields a strictly larger objective, a contradiction. (4) Weighted and cycle corollaries are derived from the theorem via a blow-up/duality (Farkas) argument and short counting. I checked steps (1)-(3) line by line and found no gap; the points below are gaps in justification rather than errors.
hardest_part: The pruning lemma (Lemma pruning, Parts 3-9): the chain from a maximum matching of the auxiliary bipartite graph to a single real assignment satisfying rank L = l, rank N = t, dim ker A >= k relies on shared variables a_{pi}, b_{sj} appearing in several matrices, and on the non-vanishing of a product of block minors in R[a,b]. I verified each block-determinant argument and the kernel restriction (Lemma kernel-support applied to W^{p,i}), but these are long and the genericity step is the easiest place for a subtle dependence to hide. The global claim (resolving a long-open conjecture) also needs independent verification beyond a local reading.

main_result: Every nonempty finite oriented graph D has a vertex v with |N_1^+(v)| <= |N_2^+(v)|, where N_2^+(v) is the set of vertices at directed distance exactly two (Seymour's second neighbourhood conjecture). The manuscript also claims weighted forms (weighted vertex and arc versions, and a normalized vertex weighting) and two directed-cycle consequences (non-neighbour bound, a 3-cycle minimum-degree result, and n >= 3*rho+1 for regular digraphs of girth 4).
proof_strategy: Proof by contradiction. A minimal counterexample D (fewest vertices, then fewest arcs) is shown to be strongly connected with positive indegrees, and for every nonempty proper S it satisfies |F^2(S)\F(S)| < |F(S)\S| (Lemma subset-deficit, via an arc-deletion argument that gives an increment inequality summed along a chain of sets). A lexicographic blow-up by transitive tournaments turns this into a strict inequality |U| + |F^2(U)| < 2|F(U)| for all proper nonempty U (Lemma blow-up). Proposition no-concavity rules out any such graph by an extremal argument on pairs of compatible families of ordered pairs, using a pruning lemma whose proof bounds a maximum matching of an auxiliary bipartite graph via generic rank (Edmonds-type) arguments and Konig's theorem. The weighted and cycle corollaries are derived from the theorem by specialization, a Farkas alternative with reversal, and direct counting. I checked each displayed inequality in the subset-deficit, blow-up, pruning and no-concavity arguments and found no algebraic or logical error, but I did not verify it by computer and I cannot independently confirm that the overall argument is correct for a problem of this kind.
hardest_part: The pruning lemma (Parts 3 to 9): the choice of one real assignment that makes the three rank conditions hold simultaneously, the kernel-restriction Claim 8 that feeds dim ker A >= k, and the matching-to-cover bookkeeping. I traced each step and found it consistent, but the genericity argument mixes shared variables across several matrices and I would not trust my check of it without a machine verification. The increment bookkeeping (5e)-(5h) in the subset-deficit lemma was the second hardest; I checked the set identities by hand.

main_result: Claims that every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex v with |N_1^+(v)| <= |N_2^+(v)|, where N_2^+(v) excludes v and N_1^+(v). This is Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture, which I believe is open as of my knowledge. The manuscript also gives weighted forms (arc-weighted, vertex-weighted with a probability weighting, and a matrix/Farkas form) and directed-triangle-free degree and order corollaries. I checked each step I could and found no false step. I cannot certify from reading alone that the whole argument resolves the open conjecture.
proof_strategy: Minimal counterexample D (fewest vertices, then fewest arcs). Lemma subset-deficit: for every nonempty proper S, |F^2(S)\F(S)| < |F(S)\S|. The proof deletes arcs from S into E\T to get a smaller non-counterexample, takes a witness v that must lose an out-neighbour, and bounds the change in g by a telescoping increment argument. Lemma blowup: lexicographic product with a transitive tournament turns that integer deficit into a strict inequality |U|+|F^2(U)|<2|F(U)| for all proper nonempty U (the case S=V(D) is handled separately using positive indegree). Proposition no-concavity: take a compatible pair (P,Q) of pair-families maximizing |P|+|Q|+uncovered, take complements of the second images to get a larger but possibly conflicting pair (R,C), and prune it with a König-plus-generic-rank pruning lemma (|deleted| <= |H| + uncovered after pruning). The pruned pair then has a larger objective, a contradiction. The weighted corollaries follow from the main theorem via a reversal and Farkas alternative, plus a direct check of the arc-weighted form.
hardest_part: The pruning lemma (Parts 3-10 of its proof). It needs the generic-rank argument with the matrices L, N, B, A, the choice of one real assignment avoiding all polynomial zeros, the kernel restriction via Lemma kernel-support, and the chain |H| >= k + ell + t - |Z|. I checked each of these step by step and they hold as written, but the argument is long and combines several block-by-block genericity arguments, so I would trust my check least here. The extremal argument in Proposition no-concavity depends on this lemma, so it is the piece I would most want an expert to recheck.
